highlight.title: Building Psychological Safety in High Performing Teams
highlight.summary: Research from Harvard Business Review (2024) reveals that psychological safety works best when paired with high performance expectations, debunking the myth that safety means lowering standards. Teams with high psychological safety maintain higher standards because feedback flows freely, creating the optimal zone where safety and accountability combine for peak performance.

resources.title: Mitigating Cognitive Bias to Improve Organizational Decisions
resources.why_now: New research from LSE, King's College London and Bayes Business School provides the first comprehensive framework integrating findings from 100 experimental studies on evidence-based bias mitigation strategies. Essential reading as leaders face increasingly complex decision-making in volatile environments.

resources.title: The Art of 21st-Century Leadership: From Succession Planning to Building a Leadership Factory
resources.why_now: McKinsey's latest research identifies six critical leadership traits for the current uncertain environment, moving beyond traditional succession planning to a 'leadership factory' model. Companies with decisive leaders who commit to decisions are 4.2 times more likely to be organizationally healthy.

resources.title: A Framework for Accelerated Leadership Development in the Workplace
resources.why_now: This March 2024 peer-reviewed research presents the first holistic framework addressing the gap between program design inputs and outcomes in leadership development. Offers practical solutions for organizations struggling to develop leaders effectively in rapidly changing business environments.

resources.title: Psychological Safety in Interdisciplinary Teams: How Leadership Behaviors Empower Teams
resources.why_now: This 2024 study provides concrete strategies for leaders to cultivate awareness, share leadership, and create structured reflection moments that strengthen psychological safety. Particularly relevant as teams become more cross-functional and collaborative work becomes increasingly complex.

claude_take: The myth that psychological safety means being 'soft' continues to damage organizations—the research clearly shows it's the opposite. Leaders who master the balance between safety and accountability create environments where tough feedback flows freely and standards remain high, making this the defining leadership challenge of our time.
